text: A package MUST include the handlers referenced by its agents. Packers discover a tool's named invocation dependencies from its `uses` declaration. A package MUST include the required tool dependencies declared there.

A packed agent's required behavior must be expressible through surfaces defined by this specification. Packed definitions MUST NOT require private runtime RPCs, implementation-specific storage schemas or bindings, undocumented events, sidecar services that substitute for runtime behavior, or `_notPackableRuntimeContext`.

Runtime-specific enhancements MAY be capability-detected and optional, but the package's declared agents and required dependencies MUST execute correctly when those enhancements are absent. When an agent category needs a new runtime primitive, that primitive belongs in the specification and its conformance surface rather than in a product-private package/runtime agreement.

Authentication, billing, deployment, and branded client services may remain outside an agent package. They MUST NOT be necessary for the installed agent's core execution semantics unless the package explicitly declares the external service as part of the agent's purpose rather than as a replacement for a missing runtime capability.
The `keywords` array MUST include `"standardagent"` for discovery.

Packers MUST include every hook referenced by an entry agent's `parentHooks`, even when no prompt or agent `hooks` array references it, and MUST reproduce those declarations in both `__meta.parentHooks` and `package.json.standardagent.parentHooks`. Hook code remains inert after package installation; the declarations activate only when a host composes the entry agent into an enabled direct child relationship.
Package names SHOULD start with `standardagent-`
Only expose agents that should be callable from outside as entry points
Internal helper agents SHOULD NOT be entry points
Requests beneath the thread endpoint prefix that do not match any local or packed thread endpoint route MUST return HTTP 404.

A GitHub Actions workflow should run when an issue opens and send it to an authenticated thread endpoint using an API key. The agent should treat issue text as data, apply a category and priority label, post a one-sentence explanation on GitHub, and end each session while keeping the thread available for the next issue.

Runtimes MUST treat provider extensions as separate provider identities from their base providers.

A provider extension MAY be defined when an API is compatible with an existing provider package but requires a distinct name, API key, base URL, model list, icons, tools, pricing, or request behavior.
A model definition MAY reference the extension provider:
Provider config values MAY include: API keys
Provider config values MAY include: base URLs
Provider config values MAY include: regions
Provider config values MAY include: account IDs
Provider config values MAY include: deployment IDs
Provider config values MAY include: request timeouts
Provider config values MAY include: default request headers (`defaultHeaders`)

A provider extension's `config` object chooses where each slot gets its value. If a slot is not overridden, the base provider's `defaultEnv` and `default` are used. For example, an OpenAI-based extension that only overrides `baseUrl` still uses `OPENAI_API_KEY`; to use its own key, the extension MUST override `apiKey`.

A config slot MAY be a nested map whose leaves are individual config values, letting a single slot combine environment and constant entries. The `defaultHeaders` slot uses this form to declare per-request headers, mixing secret env values with constant ones. When a leaf resolves to no value — an optional environment variable that is unset — that leaf is omitted rather than sent as an empty value.

`defaultHeaders` is a connection-level slot that HTTP-client provider implementations SHOULD forward on every request, so a provider extension can target an API-compatible backend that requires additional headers (account ids, API betas, relay authentication) without overriding a method.
An override MUST call `next()` to compose with the base provider. If it does not call `next()`, it replaces the base provider behavior.
API keys and other credentials MUST be declared as provider config slots or provider extension value sources with `type`/`valueType: 'secret'`.
Runtimes and setup UIs SHOULD: mark secret values as sensitive
Runtimes and setup UIs SHOULD: avoid logging raw secret values
Runtimes and setup UIs SHOULD: report missing required provider variables before model execution
Runtimes and setup UIs SHOULD: allow compatible provider extensions to use their own secret variables instead of the base provider's default key
An OpenAI model MAY use `OPENAI_API_KEY` while an OpenAI-compatible extension uses `EXAMPLE_PROVIDER_API_KEY` and `EXAMPLE_PROVIDER_BASE_URL`.
The runtime MUST: execute one step at a time per thread
The runtime MUST: persist messages and tool results before continuing
The runtime MUST: enforce configured limits and stop semantics
The runtime MUST: support queued work for idle and active threads

The runtime MUST expose `ThreadState.decide()` in accordance with [Decisions](/0.2.0/specification/threads/decisions). Decision invocation is independent of conversation execution and MUST be available when `state.execution` is `null`. Its request, result, provider configuration, and conversation semantics are defined by that contract.
For a prompt-backed side, each execution step MUST run in order: Drain queued messages/tools for this step
For a prompt-backed side, each execution step MUST run in order: Assemble LLM message context
For a prompt-backed side, each execution step MUST run in order: Call the selected model
For a prompt-backed side, each execution step MUST run in order: Persist assistant response
For a prompt-backed side, each execution step MUST run in order: Execute tool calls sequentially
For a prompt-backed side, each execution step MUST run in order: Persist tool results
For a prompt-backed side, each execution step MUST run in order: Evaluate stop conditions
Each model-context assembly MUST proceed in this order: Interpolate the system prompt
Each model-context assembly MUST proceed in this order: Invoke `after_system_message` with the rendered system message
Each model-context assembly MUST proceed in this order: Take a stable snapshot of eligible persisted history
Each model-context assembly MUST proceed in this order: Invoke `filter_messages` exactly once on that snapshot
Each model-context assembly MUST proceed in this order: Transform the filtered result into provider messages
Each model-context assembly MUST proceed in this order: Invoke `prefilter_llm_history`
Each model-context assembly MUST proceed in this order: Dispatch the provider request

The snapshot MUST be the set of eligible persisted messages at the moment the runtime starts `filter_messages`. Messages persisted before that moment MUST be eligible for the current assembly. Messages injected after that moment MUST become eligible for the following assembly.

`injectMessage()` MUST NOT restart steps 3–6. Live execution history stays independent of the request context. See [Messages §3](/0.2.0/specification/threads/messages#3-injecting-messages) and [Hooks §3.4](/0.2.0/specification/hooks#34-stored-history-and-the-request-context).
Tool calls MUST execute sequentially in the returned order.
Tool errors MUST be persisted as tool results and MUST NOT crash the execution loop.
Runtimes MUST support: function tools
Runtimes MUST support: prompt tools
Runtimes MUST support: agent handoff tools (exposed agents with a human side)
Runtimes MUST support: runtime-injected subagent lifecycle tools (`subagents`, `subagent_create`, `subagent_message`) for sides with declared relationships
Stop evaluation order should be: `sessionStop` / `sessionFail` terminal lifecycle tools
Stop evaluation order should be: `stopTool`
Stop evaluation order should be: `stopOnResponse`
Stop evaluation order should be: safety limits (`maxSteps`, `maxSessionTurns`, runtime hard caps)
Runtimes MUST: create child threads with parent linkage
Runtimes MUST: maintain child registry entries, keyed by relationship name (`as`), for child instances
Runtimes MUST: expose parent/child lookup through `ThreadState`
Creation attempts beyond `maxInstances` MUST return tool errors with actionable guidance.

The effective `parentCommunication` mode is the relationship's `parentCommunication`, defaulting to `implicit`. When the effective mode is `explicit`, runtimes MUST NOT auto-queue child completion/failure to the parent — and because that queued message is what schedules a parent turn, an `explicit` child's completion does not wake the parent. Runtimes should persist the effective mode on the child registry entry so both the parent-side and child-side completion paths can honor it.
Runtimes should evaluate relationship flags before exposing/executing them: `optional`: only enabled when the referenced environment flag resolves to `true`, `1`, or `yes` (case-insensitive)

Runtimes should evaluate relationship flags before exposing/executing them: `immediate`: spawn at thread creation, before any side takes a turn — even when the owning side is a handler, and even when the first inbound message arrives immediately

Runtimes should evaluate relationship flags before exposing/executing them: `immediate` object form: treat `nameEnv` and `descriptionEnv` as safe bootstrap hints and `scopedEnv` as runtime-only transfer data

Runtimes should evaluate relationship flags before exposing/executing them: `hidden`: the relationship stays declared and spawnable by runtime code (`invokeTool`/`queueTool` from hooks, tools, and handlers), but the tool MUST NOT appear in any LLM request's tool list — for infrastructure children (e.g. background context compaction) the model must never invoke itself
Immediate spawning should be recursive across activated child threads.

For each active prompt, runtimes MUST resolve the complete thread-hook set from the side's enabled direct subagent relationships before a hook position runs. Resolution is declarative and does not require the child thread to have been spawned. Installed packages that are not added to a prompt contribute nothing.

Child requirements load from the implementing child's package namespace and execute against the parent thread. Resolution MUST fail closed if a required hook cannot be loaded or is user-scoped. The same composition applies to every thread hook position, including `after_thread_created`; runtimes must not special-case a subset of hook types.

Within one hook position, runtimes MUST run child `before_parent` hooks in prompt tool order and declaration order, then the parent's effective prompt-or- agent hook set, then child `after_parent` hooks in the same stable order.
For runtime lifecycle creation, `subagent_create` must receive a non-empty `name` argument and runtimes should persist that name for child thread display.

`subagent_create.arguments` should be validated against the `requiredSchema` of the child's side A prompt — parent traffic enters the child in the side B perspective (`role: 'user'`), so side A acts on it, exactly as for an external caller. Runtimes must persist those initial arguments with the child thread's metadata/properties and expose them to both child sides on future executions through `ThreadState.arguments` and the prompt render flow: top-level argument keys are available to prompt variable interpolation for whichever side is currently rendering, including included prompts.
`scopedEnv` values must remain encrypted at rest and runtime-only during transfer
copied child env must never be injected into LLM-visible prompt text unless explicitly promoted through `nameEnv` or `descriptionEnv`

If `subagent_create` cannot proceed because required scoped variables are missing, runtimes should return a structured bootstrap error and expose a temporary completion flow: `GET /threads/{parent_thread_id}/variables/{request_id}`

If `subagent_create` cannot proceed because required scoped variables are missing, runtimes should return a structured bootstrap error and expose a temporary completion flow: `POST /threads/{parent_thread_id}/variables/{request_id}`
referenced attachments MUST be copied parent filesystem -> child filesystem
queued child messages must use child-local attachment paths
payload attachments MUST be copied child filesystem -> parent filesystem
parent message content should include subagent reference and result summary

`state.stopSession()` marks the active session terminal without requiring a `sessionStop` tool call. Implementations should treat this as a successful terminal child run for blocking and non-blocking subagent lifecycle handling. The optional `notifyParent` and `status` fields perform the same parent-message and registry-status effects as `notifyParent()` and `setStatus()`.
persistence should survive DO eviction

Session end — stop, fail, error, or turn-cap — MUST NOT terminate a child thread; only explicit termination destroys an instance. Retention of idle threads (archival, eviction, listing policy) is runtime-defined and out of scope for this specification.
A single thread MUST NOT execute multiple concurrent flows. Cross-thread concurrency is allowed.

When implemented, runtime streams are live, non-durable resources authorized by the runtime. Capability names and metadata remain opaque to the shared runtime layer. Streams must route to the selected execution host, must not park, and must terminate when that host disconnects. See the complete [Runtime Streams contract](/0.2.0/specification/threads/runtime-streams).
A conforming implementation MUST: Create a fresh isolate per `runCode` call. No module cache, intrinsic, or top-level binding leaks across calls.

A conforming implementation MUST: Present a `globalThis` containing only ECMAScript intrinsics. Host APIs (`fetch`, `setTimeout`, `console`, `process`, `require`, etc.) MUST NOT be present unless the caller installed them via `options.globals`.
A conforming implementation MUST: Install `options.globals` identifiers at module scope only — they MUST NOT appear on `globalThis` or be enumerable via `Object.keys(globalThis)`.

A conforming implementation MUST: Freshly construct the sandbox's intrinsic prototypes; mutating `Object.prototype`, `Array.prototype`, or any other intrinsic inside the sandbox MUST have zero effect on the host.

A conforming implementation MUST: Reject `eval`, `new Function(source)`, `SharedArrayBuffer`, `Atomics`, and URL dynamic imports. Relative dynamic imports may resolve only when the target is supplied through `options.modules`.

Bare specifiers resolve only from `options.imports`. Relative specifiers resolve only from `options.modules`. Unknown specifiers and URL specifiers (`https://…`) MUST fail linkage and settle with `status: 'link_error'`.
`import.meta.url` MUST be a synthetic `sandbox:<filename>` URL. Host paths MUST NOT be exposed.
Class instances, `WeakMap`, `WeakRef`, and symbols with host identity are not transferable. Runtimes MAY throw a `SerializationError`.
Bridged functions MUST NOT expose host `this` or host closure state to the sandbox beyond their explicit arguments.

Memory: when the engine supports heap accounting, the runtime MUST enforce `options.memoryLimitBytes` and settle with `status: 'memory'` on overrun. When `memoryLimitBytes` is omitted, a runtime-defined default applies; the runtime SHOULD document it. Implementations MAY impose a platform-fixed ceiling that caller values cannot exceed. When a caller requests a limit above that ceiling, runtimes MUST either (a) clamp to the ceiling and settle overruns with `status: 'memory'` and an `error.message` naming the effective limit, or (b) reject the call with `status: 'link_error'` naming the cap. Runtimes MUST document which behavior they use and the effective ceiling.

Termination: `handle.terminate()` MUST signal the sandbox to stop. The handle MUST settle at the next ECMAScript yield point (microtask boundary, async operation, or runtime interrupt) — SHOULD be within 50 ms and typically a few. A sandbox running a pure-synchronous tight loop may not reach a yield point; runtimes MAY rely on their own safety cap (next bullet) to force settlement. `terminate` is idempotent; subsequent calls are no-ops. When the caller passes `reason`, it surfaces in `result.error.message`.

Safety caps (optional): runtimes MAY apply their own caps (for example, interrupting a pure-JS infinite loop under sustained CPU pressure). When a cap fires, the handle settles with `status: 'terminated'` and a diagnosable `error.message` — the same channel as caller-initiated termination.
The spec does not require a wall-clock timeout. Runtimes MUST NOT invent one silently; callers impose deadlines by calling `handle.terminate()`.
After module evaluation, the runtime MUST resolve the export selected by `options.execute` in this order: Read `module.namespace[execute.fn]`, where `execute.fn` defaults to `'default'`.

After module evaluation, the runtime MUST resolve the export selected by `options.execute` in this order: If it is a function, call it with `execute.args` inside the sandbox. The return value is the new candidate for step 3.
After module evaluation, the runtime MUST resolve the export selected by `options.execute` in this order: If the current candidate is a thenable, await it. Repeat until the value is not a thenable.
After module evaluation, the runtime MUST resolve the export selected by `options.execute` in this order: Marshal the final value into `CodeExecutionResult.result`.

If the selected export is missing, the runtime MUST settle with `status: 'link_error'`. If the selected export is not a function and `execute.args` is non-empty, the runtime MUST settle with `status: 'error'`. An uncaught throw from the selected-export function (or a rejection from its returned promise) MUST settle with `status: 'error'`.

When `options.language === 'typescript'` (the default), the runtime MUST strip types before evaluation. Runtimes SHOULD use a type-erasure implementation (`sucrase`, `esbuild-transform`, `swc`, or native type-stripping). Runtimes MUST NOT invoke a TypeScript type-checker as part of `runCode` — only erasure runs.
A runtime that implements code execution MUST: Expose `ThreadState.runCode(source, options?)` returning a `CodeExecution` handle.
A runtime that implements code execution MUST: Accept TypeScript source by default and evaluate it as an ES module.
A runtime that implements code execution MUST: Resolve bare-specifier imports only from `options.imports`, relative imports only from `options.modules`, and fail linkage on URL or unknown specifiers.
A runtime that implements code execution MUST: Install `options.globals` at module scope but not on `globalThis`.
A runtime that implements code execution MUST: Present an isolated `globalThis` with only ECMAScript intrinsics.
A runtime that implements code execution MUST: Reject `eval`, `new Function(source)`, `SharedArrayBuffer`, `Atomics`, and URL dynamic imports.
A runtime that implements code execution MUST: Enforce `options.memoryLimitBytes` when the engine supports heap accounting; settle with `status: 'memory'` on overrun.
A runtime that implements code execution MUST: Settle the handle with `status: 'terminated'` within 50 ms of `handle.terminate()`.
A runtime that implements code execution MUST: Marshal values across the boundary by structured clone / callable proxy, with no shared references.
A runtime that implements code execution MUST: Resolve the configured export per [§14.5](#145-configured-export-resolution).

A runtime that implements code execution MUST: Return `CodeExecutionResult` with the exact status codes defined in the [caller-facing spec](/0.2.0/specification/threads/code-execution#41-status-values).
A runtime that implements code execution MUST: Create a fresh isolate per call; leak no state between calls.
A runtime SHOULD: Capture `console.*` logs when no `console` global is supplied.
A runtime SHOULD: Surface syntactic and linker errors with `line`/`column` pointing to the caller's source.
A runtime SHOULD: Call `handle.terminate()` when `state.execution?.abortSignal` fires.

`ThreadState.getValue` / `ThreadState.setValue` expose a simple durable key-value store scoped to the thread. The caller-facing surface is specified in [Threads §7](/0.2.0/specification/threads#7-durable-key-value-store); the runtime semantics below define how implementations must back it.
Values MUST be persisted to durable per-thread storage that survives execution boundaries, process restarts, and runtime redeploys.
A value written by `setValue(key, value)` MUST be visible to every subsequent `getValue(key)` on the same thread, across any execution context (tools, hooks, endpoints).
Each thread MUST maintain its own isolated key space. Values MUST NOT be readable by any other thread, including parent, child, or sibling threads.
Values MUST round-trip with JSON-equivalent structure (objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, `null`). Runtimes MAY reject non-JSON-serializable values with a thrown error.
`getValue(key)` MUST return `null` when no value has been set for the key, when the value has been deleted, or when the thread is accessed after the store has never been written.
`setValue(key, null)` and `setValue(key, undefined)` MUST delete the key so that subsequent `getValue(key)` calls return `null`.
Writes SHOULD be durable before the promise returned by `setValue` resolves.
Values MUST NOT be automatically copied, inherited, or synchronized between threads when subagents are spawned.
Storage is not required to be encrypted at rest (unlike `env`); runtimes MAY encrypt at their discretion.

Runtimes MAY enforce implementation-defined caps on key length, value size, and total number of keys per thread. When a cap is exceeded, `setValue` SHOULD reject with an error that identifies which limit was hit. Caps SHOULD be documented with the runtime.

A runtime SHOULD expose the [Thread Client API](/0.2.0/specification/threads/client-api): HTTP routes to list agents, create, list, read, update, and delete threads, read, send, and delete messages, read thread files, and stop execution, plus a WebSocket thread stream and the stream tickets that authorize it. These routes and frames are fixed by the specification so that one client works against any conforming runtime.
A runtime that exposes the API MUST: mount every specified route beneath `{runtime_prefix}`

A runtime that exposes the API MUST: authenticate every request, accept bearer credentials on HTTP routes and single-use stream tickets on the stream upgrade, and enforce its thread access policy on thread-addressed routes
A runtime that exposes the API MUST: return a `5xx` status, never a client-error status, for internal failures
A runtime that exposes the API MUST: set a created thread's owner from the authenticated caller
A runtime that exposes the API MUST: accept a sent message durably and respond before the resulting execution completes
A runtime that exposes the API MUST: send a `thread_status` snapshot as the first frame of every stream connection, and again on every run status change
A runtime that exposes the API MUST: publish message creations and updates as `message_data` frames, streamed assistant content as `message_chunk` frames, and `state.emit` calls as `event` frames
A runtime that exposes the API MUST: withhold `reasoning_chunk` frames from connections that did not opt in
A runtime that exposes the API MUST: persist the reasoning a model returns with an assistant message, and carry it in the message record on reads and on the stream
A runtime that exposes the API MUST: on thread deletion, make the thread and its descendants unavailable to new work, abort and discard their work, and close their streams before confirming
A runtime that exposes the API MUST: apply each connection's `depth` and `includeSilent` filters
A runtime that exposes the API MUST: answer the `stream_ping` text frame with `stream_pong`
Implementations MUST: preserve sequential step and tool execution within a thread
Implementations MUST: enforce stop and safety semantics
Implementations MUST: persist messages/tool results before advancing
Implementations MUST: prevent per-thread concurrent execution
Implementations MUST: support durable queue semantics
Implementations MUST: copy attachment files across thread boundaries for subagent communication
Implementations MUST: honor the [Code Execution](#13-code-execution-runtime) runtime contract when `ThreadState.runCode` is exposed
Implementations MUST: back `ThreadState.getValue` / `ThreadState.setValue` with a durable, per-thread key-value store per [§14](#14-durable-key-value-store)
Implementations SHOULD: expose the [Thread Client API](#15-thread-client-api)
A side's configuration is discriminated by its backing: exactly one of `human`, `prompt`, or `handler` MUST be present.
An exposed agent MAY declare thread-scoped hooks that are required for the composed relationship to work correctly:

Downloading or installing a package is inert. Declaring a `SubagentRelationship` targeting the agent (or adding it to an enabled parent prompt as a handoff) is what composes it, and composing it MUST activate every `parentHooks` requirement automatically. A second accept-list is not required: composition UIs MUST disclose the hook ID, reason, and stage before the relationship is added or enabled.
Any agent with `exposeAsTool: true` MAY declare `parentHooks` — any agent is composable, so any exposed agent may carry composition requirements.
Missing, invalid, or unloadable required hooks MUST fail composition closed. Runtimes must not silently run a partially installed child.

Implementations MUST reject the following at definition time: Both sides human — reserved. The mediated human↔human thread is coherent and the restriction may lift in a later version, but 0.2.0 runtimes MUST reject it.
Implementations MUST reject the following at definition time: `subagents` declared on a human-backed side.
Implementations MUST reject the following at definition time: A side with zero backings, or more than one of `human` / `prompt` / `handler`.
Implementations MUST reject the following at definition time: A handler side referencing an undefined handler; a prompt side referencing an undefined prompt.

Implementations MUST reject the following at definition time: A relationship name (`as`) appearing on both sides of one agent, colliding with another tool name, or colliding with a reserved lifecycle tool name — see [Subagents §2](/0.2.0/specification/subagents#2-ownership-rules).
Implementations MUST reject the following at definition time: Session bindings (`sessionStop` / `sessionFail` / `sessionStatus`), `maxSteps`, or stop bindings on a non-prompt side.
Implementations MUST reject the following at definition time: A session binding that is not in object form ([§3](#3-sessiontoolbinding)).
Validation issues SHOULD be reported as a structured list (`code`, `severity`, `message`, `path`) so tooling can surface every problem in one pass.

Effects are scheduled side-effect handlers that run outside normal tool execution. They are ideal for delayed notifications, background cleanup, and async operations that should not block a model step.
Effects MUST be declared with `defineEffect()` and exported as the default export from a file in `agents/effects/`.
Names SHOULD use `snake_case`
Names MUST be unique within the active namespace
Runtimes should support [qualified names](/0.2.0/distribution/packaging#qualified-names) for packed effects.
MUST enqueue effects asynchronously for execution.
MUST preserve scheduled `args` until execution time.
SHOULD expose inspection and cancellation APIs (`getScheduledEffects`, `removeScheduledEffect`).
SHOULD keep effect handlers idempotent.

Handlers MUST NOT be referenced by prompt `tools` arrays, hook lists, or effect schedules. Implementations MUST reject such references at definition time. This keeps the taxonomy crisp — code that wants a capability writes a tool; code that wants to decorate writes a hook; code that owns turns is a handler.
The runtime MUST invoke the handler exactly once for each inbound message on the side's perspective, in message persistence order.

The runtime MUST NOT invoke a handler concurrently for the same thread. Messages that arrive while a handler turn is in flight MUST wait in the queue and be delivered one at a time, in order, after the current turn completes.
The runtime MUST NOT automatically redeliver a message whose handler invocation failed. Retry is a userland decision (re-send the message).

> Warning: Because queued messages wait behind the in-flight turn, a long-running handler stalls its thread. In particular, a handler that awaits a `blocking` child session holds the delivery slot for that session's entire duration — and if that child can only finish after *another* inbound message on this thread, the thread deadlocks. Relay-style handlers SHOULD forward without blocking (`queueMessage` toward the child) and treat the child's replies as ordinary later turns.
The turn is marked failed. The error MUST be surfaced on the runtime's request/execution log as a runtime-origin failure — a throwing handler never silently swallows a message.

This is deliberately unlike hooks (whose failures are non-fatal to the turn they decorate) and unlike session failure (`sessionFail` / `stopSession`), which a handler must invoke explicitly if an error should end the session.

Handlers get no auto-injected reply channel. If a handler (or the side it feeds) should speak to a user or an external surface, that is userland code — a tool or handler calling the messaging surface it chooses (the `message_user` pattern).
Each hook implementation MUST be created using `defineHook()` with three properties: | `hook` | `HookName` | The hook type from §1.1 |
Each hook implementation MUST be created using `defineHook()` with three properties: | `id` | `string` | Unique identifier for this hook (snake_case) |
Each hook implementation MUST be created using `defineHook()` with three properties: | `execute` | `Function` | The hook implementation (typed per hook type) |
The `hook` property MUST reference one of the hook types in §1.1.
The `id` property MUST be unique across all hooks and follow `snake_case` format.
Multiple hooks of the same type MAY exist, each with a distinct `id`.
Hook implementations SHOULD be idempotent.
Runtimes SHOULD enforce a timeout on hook execution.
Hooks SHOULD NOT perform blocking operations that could exceed that timeout.
Hooks MUST NOT expose sensitive data in logs or error messages.

Child hook IDs resolve in the child's package namespace and execute with the parent's `ThreadState`. A missing, invalid, unloadable, or user-scoped required hook MUST fail composition closed. See [Agents §6](/0.2.0/specification/agents#6-required-parent-hooks).

`relationshipName` is the relationship name (`as`, defaulting to the agent name); `agentName` is the resolved implementing agent. Package provenance, when present, MUST identify the namespace from which the child hook was loaded. Prompt and agent hooks receive their corresponding prompt/agent source. This context is deterministic runtime metadata and must not be inferred from mutable thread data.
Implementations MUST invoke this hook after system-prompt interpolation and before the history snapshot.
A returned string MUST replace the rendered system message for the current request.
`null` or `undefined` MUST leave the current system message unchanged.
A message injected here is persisted before the snapshot. It MUST be eligible for the current assembly and MUST pass through `filter_messages`.

Relationship names share the tool namespace. A relationship name that collides with another tool name is a definition-time error, and the injected lifecycle tool names — `subagents`, `subagent_create`, `subagent_message` — are explicitly reserved: a colliding `as` MUST be rejected with a dedicated validation code.

When `blocking: true` is combined with `maxInstances: 1` and an instance already exists, `subagent_create` MUST behave as create-or-continue: message the existing instance and await *that* session's close, rather than erroring on the cap. This is what callers invariably mean by "run the child again."

Session end never terminates a thread. When a child session ends — stop, fail, error, or turn-cap — the registry status transitions (`running` → `idle` / `failed`), the thread remains addressable, and a later message starts a new session with history intact. Runtimes MUST NOT destroy or orphan child threads on any session-finalization path.

Child visibility is pull-based: runtimes inject the `subagents` query tool ([§5](#5-lifecycle-tools)) and MUST NOT additionally inject an ambient registry system message — a registry block that mutates between requests invalidates provider prefix caches and reads as out-of-dialogue state. Completions arrive as messages.

`subagents` — the pull-based visibility surface. Takes no arguments; returns the registry snapshot for the side's relationships — reference, relationship name, agent name, status, working-status text, initial arguments, creation time. Injected tool descriptions SHOULD direct the model to call `subagents` before `subagent_create` so existing instances are reused rather than duplicated.

`subagent_create` — creates (or continues, [§3.3](#33-blocking-and-create-or-continue)) an instance. Its `agent` argument MUST enumerate the side's enabled relationship *names*. It MUST require a non-empty `name` argument for the spawned instance; runtimes SHOULD persist this as a human-readable child thread display name.

All lifecycle references use relationship names, never an internal agent identifier that differs from them. Runtimes MUST reject lifecycle invocations that target undeclared or disabled relationships without creating a child.

runtimes MUST validate them against the schema and persist the validated arguments for the life of the child thread.

runtimes MUST hydrate them into `ThreadState.arguments` and prompt variable interpolation for both child sides on every activation — the initial invocation and every later resume — so spawn-time context (a stylist child that needs sizes and preferences, say) is available for as long as the thread lives.
if required arguments are missing, runtimes MUST reject creation with a structured `subagent_arguments_required` error rather than spawning the child.

A successful request MUST return `200` with a `StreamTicketResponse` and the response header `Cache-Control: no-store`.

The runtime MUST return `400` when `pathname` is absent, is not a normalized path beneath `{runtime_prefix}`, or contains a query or fragment. A path is normalized when it has no `.` or `..` segment, no empty segment, no trailing slash, and no percent-encoded `.`, `/`, or `\` (`%2E`, `%2F`, `%5C`, in either letter case).
The runtime MUST authenticate an upgrade that presents a valid ticket as the caller who requested the ticket.
A ticket MUST be valid only for an upgrade whose path equals `pathname`. The comparison is of the exact strings.
A ticket MUST be valid for at most one upgrade.
A ticket MUST expire no later than `expires_in` seconds after it is issued. `expires_in` SHOULD NOT exceed `60`.
The runtime MUST reject an upgrade that presents an unknown, expired, used, or mismatched ticket with `401`.
A ticket authorizes a stream upgrade only. The runtime MUST NOT accept it as a bearer credential.
A successful request MUST return `200` with an `AgentList`.
The runtime MUST accept every listed `id` as the `agent_id` of a create request (§6) from the same caller.
`title` MUST be the agent's `title`, or its `name` when the agent defines no title.
`primary` MUST be `false` when the [agent definition](/0.2.0/specification/agents#22-optional) sets `primary: false`, and `true` otherwise.
`side_a_backing` and `side_b_backing` MUST report the [backing](/0.2.0/specification/agents) of each side.
A request without `primary` MUST return the whole creatable set, and no other agent.
A request that sets `primary=true` MUST return exactly the agents of the creatable set whose `primary` is `true`.
The runtime MUST set the owner of the new thread from the authenticated caller. The request MUST NOT be able to name a different owner.
Creating a thread MUST NOT start an execution.
A successful request MUST return `200` with a `CreateThreadResponse`.

The runtime MUST return `400` when `agent_id` is absent or is not a string, when `tags` is present and is not an array of strings, or when `env` is present and is not a JSON object whose values are all strings.
The runtime MUST return `404` when `agent_id` is a string that is not the `id` of an agent in the caller's creatable set (§5). A filter on an agent list request does not change that set.
A successful request MUST return `200` with a `ThreadList`.
A caller without administrative rights MUST receive only threads that the caller owns.

The runtime MUST return threads in descending `last_activity_at` order unless the request selects another order through a runtime-defined parameter. The order of threads with equal `last_activity_at` is runtime-defined.
`total` MUST be the number of threads matching the request before `limit` and `offset` are applied.
`hasMore` MUST be `true` if and only if matching threads exist beyond the returned page.
`last_activity_at` MUST equal `created_at` for a thread with no later activity.
`agent.title` MUST be the agent's `name` when the agent defines no title or its definition is no longer available.
A successful request MUST return `200` with a `ThreadRead`.
`status` MUST equal the [`ThreadStatus`](/0.2.0/specification/threads/execution-state#4-run-status) that `state.status()` resolves for the thread.
`agent` MUST be `null` when the thread's agent definition is no longer available.
When `tags` is present, the runtime MUST replace the thread's tags with the given array.
A successful request MUST return `200` with an `UpdateThreadResponse` that reflects the update.
The runtime MUST return `400` when `tags` is not an array of strings, or when the request names no field the runtime updates.

Before it deletes anything, the runtime MUST make every thread in the deletion set unavailable to new work. From that point each such thread MUST reject new messages, MUST NOT start an execution, and MUST NOT create a child thread.
A child thread created beneath a thread in the deletion set before requirement 1 takes effect MUST be part of the deletion set.
The runtime MUST abort every execution in flight in the deletion set, and MUST discard every queued message and scheduled [effect](/0.2.0/specification/effects) of those threads.
The runtime MUST close every [thread stream](#16-thread-stream) connection to a thread in the deletion set with WebSocket close code `1000`.
The runtime MUST delete the messages, files, and stored values of every thread in the deletion set.
The runtime MUST return `200` with a `DeleteThreadResponse` only once requirements 1 to 5 hold. `deletedThreadIds` MUST list every thread in the deletion set, including `threadId`.

After a successful request, no execution of a deleted thread may persist state or start work, and every route addressed to a deleted thread MUST return `404`. That includes a request to its stream route that is not a WebSocket upgrade.

When deletion fails part-way, the runtime MUST return a `5xx` status (§3.2). Every thread in the deletion set MUST remain unavailable to new work, and the addressed thread MUST remain addressable so that the request can be repeated.
A repeated request MUST complete the deletion.
A successful request MUST return `200` with a `MessagesPage`.
Each entry of `messages` MUST be a [message record](/0.2.0/specification/threads/messages#1-message-structure) in its decoded form: `attachments` is an array or `null`, and `silent` is a boolean.
Under `order=desc`, the runtime MUST return the selected messages in ascending `created_at` order, so the newest selected message is last.
The runtime MUST exclude silent messages unless `includeSilent` is `true`.
The runtime MUST exclude messages whose `depth` exceeds the `depth` parameter.
Under `order=asc`, the runtime MUST return the selected messages in ascending `created_at` order.
`total` MUST be the number of messages that satisfy `includeSilent` and `depth`, before `limit` and `offset` are applied.
`hasMore` MUST be `true` if and only if matching messages exist beyond the returned page: that is, when `offset` plus the number of returned messages is less than `total`.
The order of messages with equal `created_at` is runtime-defined. It MUST be the same on every read.
The runtime MUST return `400` when `role` is absent or is not one of the three values above.
The runtime MUST return `400` when `content` is empty or absent and `attachments` is empty or absent. Content that holds only white space is empty.
The runtime MUST return `423` when the thread is terminated.

The runtime MUST send a `message_data` frame when a message is created and when a message is updated.
The runtime MUST send `message_chunk` frames for one `message_id` in generation order.
The runtime MUST NOT send a `reasoning_chunk` frame on a connection that did not opt in.

The runtime MUST NOT send a `message_data` frame for a silent message on a connection that did not set `includeSilent`.

A client MUST treat `message_data` as a replacement for any record it holds with the same `message_id`.

A runtime MAY support one packaged user room per project. A room definition is exported with `defineUserRoom` from a `users/<package>/room.ts` module, which MUST NOT also be routed as an HTTP endpoint. Room frames and presence callbacks execute under the same per-user serialization guarantee as user endpoints. Application authentication policy and proof formats belong to the room. If multiple modules declare rooms, the runtime MUST refuse room upgrades and room delivery until the ambiguity is resolved; it MUST NOT select one by import order. Independent user endpoints and event streams remain available.

The `me` form MUST resolve the authenticated user's identity. The administrative form MUST require authorization to administer the addressed user. Non-upgrade requests return HTTP 426. An accepted socket receives `{ "type": "hub_ready" }`; this acknowledges transport attachment, not application authentication.

The URL query parameters `client_id` and optional `client_kind` are self-declared text, never credentials. Each is trimmed and truncated to 256 UTF-16 code units; empty values are absent. Explicit admission requires a nonempty `client_id` after normalization, otherwise the upgrade returns HTTP 400. Automatic mode MAY accept an unidentified hub socket for runtime coordination, but it is not a room connection: it is absent from `clients()`, receives no room broadcasts, and its frames do not invoke `onFrame`.

Only text frames containing a JSON object with `type: 'room'` and a nonempty string `id` of at most 256 UTF-16 code units invoke `onFrame`. Other frames do not invoke the room. The `id` is chosen by the client to correlate replies; application replies SHOULD echo it. Other fields belong to the application protocol. The runtime does not automatically acknowledge a room frame. When no room is defined, an identified connection's valid room frame receives `{ type: 'room', id, error: 'no_room' }`. Runtimes MAY impose frame size, rate and delivery budgets, closing connections that exceed them.

Supersession sends `{ type: 'superseded' }` and closes the replaced socket with code 4001. Clients SHOULD stop automatic reconnection after this signal. Other runtime close codes are implementation-defined, except for codes explicitly requested through `roomAttachments.close`.

`UserState.clients()` lists live admitted room connections, one per client id, oldest attachment first. `UserState.send(clientId, frame)` targets the admitted connection for that id and returns false if none exists. Neither method queues traffic for an absent connection. Ordinary room admission is automatic: a new connection with the same client id replaces the previous one. Automatic-mode presence MAY coalesce reconnects within a bounded grace period. A socket retired for rate, size or send failure MUST also produce a detached event after that grace period unless an admitted replacement remains.

Explicit admission is an optional capability exposed as `UserState.roomAttachments?: UserRoomAttachments`. A consumer requiring it MUST check that this capability and `connection.attachmentId` exist and fail closed when unavailable. This capability is available during serialized room and user endpoint executions; observational hooks do not receive it. A runtime supporting `admission: 'explicit'` MUST implement all the following requirements: A new physical attachment starts pending. Its self-declared client id MUST NOT displace an admitted connection. Pending attachments MUST NOT receive client-id-targeted traffic, room broadcasts, or runtime wake traffic, and MUST NOT appear in `clients()` or count as a reachable execution client. This does not change independently authorized user event stream access.

Explicit admission is an optional capability exposed as `UserState.roomAttachments?: UserRoomAttachments`. A consumer requiring it MUST check that this capability and `connection.attachmentId` exist and fail closed when unavailable.
